one_liner: Ramp has a broad REST API with OAuth2 (client credentials and authorization code), a sandbox, and an official MCP server. Credentials need a Ramp admin account, and the API agreement says access requires Ramp review.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 with Client Credentials, Authorization Code and Refresh Token grants. The token endpoint uses HTTP Basic with the client ID and secret, but that is only for token exchange. Publishing an app to other Ramp businesses goes through the Developer console, which is partner-oriented.
access_notes: A developer app can be created in a Ramp account by an admin, and sandbox credentials are available. The API agreement says sandbox or production access requires a request for Ramp review. Publishing to other businesses needs the Developer console, which is part of the Technology Partner Program. Some scopes are partner-only.
blocker_notes: Credentials need Ramp admin access and approval under the API agreement. Multi-user distribution requires publishing through the partner Developer Console.

evidence.quote: Authorization Code | Third-party apps, public integrations | Authorized user consent required
Currently Ramp supports two grant types -- Client Credentials and Authorization Code.
To receive access to the Ramp APIs in a sandbox or production environment, you must submit a request for Ramp review.
To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.
Partners are eligible to receive referral incentives and starts with access to the Partner Portal, aggregated client insights, a co-branded referral page, and Sandbox and Developer Console access.
Ramp hosts an official remote server at `https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp` (with a sample-data variant at `https://demo-mcp.ramp.com/mcp`).
